---
title: "Readings — Barcodes, UMIs and where information lives"
---

Read these for the design argument in each: what the label has to survive, and what the authors checked to show that it did.

## Sample indexes and barcode design

**Hamady M, Walker JJ, Harris JK, Gold NJ, Knight R (2008).** *Error-correcting barcoded primers for pyrosequencing hundreds of samples in multiplex.* Nature Methods 5:235–237.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.1184](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.1184) — **start here**

> Short and clear on why barcodes must be a minimum distance apart, and how a Hamming-code-style set lets an error be corrected rather than merely noticed.

**Buschmann T, Bystrykh LV (2013).** *Levenshtein error-correcting barcodes for multiplexed DNA sequencing.* BMC Bioinformatics 14:272.
[doi:10.1186/1471-2105-14-272](https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2105-14-272)

> The same idea when the errors include insertions and deletions. Look at why the Hamming design fails when a base is lost.

**Kircher M, Sawyer S, Meyer M (2012).** *Double indexing overcomes inaccuracies in multiplex sequencing on the Illumina platform.* Nucleic Acids Research 40:e3.
[doi:10.1093/nar/gkr771](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkr771)

> The case for reading two indexes. Compare with the sequencer deck's treatment of index hopping.

**Costello M, et al. (2018).** *Characterization and remediation of sample index swaps by non-redundant dual indexing on massively parallel sequencing platforms.* BMC Genomics 19:332.
[doi:10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-018-4703-0)

> Measures the swap rate and shows what unique dual indexes remove. Look at the rates for the different flow cells.

## Cell barcodes

**Macosko EZ, et al. (2015).** *Highly parallel genome-wide expression profiling of individual cells using nanoliter droplets.* Cell 161:1202–1214.
[doi:10.1016/j.cell.2015.05.002](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2015.05.002)

> Bead-bound barcodes with a UMI on every oligo. The read structure in the methods is a good one to draw.

**Rosenberg AB, et al. (2018).** *Single-cell profiling of the developing mouse brain and spinal cord with split-pool barcoding.* Science 360:176–182.
[doi:10.1126/science.aam8999](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aam8999)

> Cell identity as a path through wells. Note how many cells can be labelled and how collisions are handled.

## UMIs and consensus

**Kivioja T, et al. (2012).** *Counting absolute numbers of molecules using unique molecular identifiers.* Nature Methods 9:72–74.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.1778](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.1778) — **start here**

> The founding argument for UMIs. Look at how the number of molecules is recovered from the number of distinct tags observed.

**Smith T, Heger A, Sudbery I (2017).** *UMI-tools: modeling sequencing errors in unique molecular identifiers to improve quantification accuracy.* Genome Research 27:491–499.
[doi:10.1101/gr.209601.116](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.209601.116)

> Why UMIs need error handling and how the network methods compare.

**Schmitt MW, et al. (2012).** *Detection of ultra-rare mutations by next-generation sequencing.* PNAS 109:14508–14513.
[doi:10.1073/pnas.1208715109](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1208715109)

> Duplex tags: a mutation must appear on both strands of the original molecule. Look at the error rate before and after.

## Reference material to keep open

- [NGS 101](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/) draws the read structure of every protocol named in the lecture.
- Your instrument's index-adapter guide: it states the colour-balance rules for your flow cell.
